title: Illinois Jacquet's gift for copying solos
summary: Cobb recalls Jacquet copying Eddie Barefield's Moonglow solo after eight months on alto, and is asked whether he is original too.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: See, Illinois had a deal. When Eddie Barefield made "Moonglow", Illinois hadn't been playing alto but 8 months -- and he copied Eddie Barefield's solo verbatim on alto; that's how sharp he was, the [nigger.]
But that was when Eddie was with Calloway?

Cab Calloway. "Moonglow". And he could pick up anything, because he -- and he can do it today. He'll copy you, and you, caught your ear and he'll get it. He'll copy anything you do - that's how sharp he is. Which is wonderful.
Is he original as well as he ghosts copies?
